reason: B is the stronger proposal because it offers a specific, non-trivial inoculation strategy with controlled loading and a decisive matched-build experiment, extending oxide-dispersion and rapid-solidification findings to cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi rather than largely restating the known preheating approach. Its proposed reductions in Si segregation and residual stress remain mechanistically uncertain—Y₂O₃ may agglomerate or introduce inclusions—but A is weakened by the questionable claim that slower cooling will refine grains and reduce segregation.
